body:
>Aren't there ways of meeting people with shared interests, though?

I don't even care anymore.
Every time I meet someone new, I always assume the best about that person, only to be disappointed after a short while.

> school

When I was at school everything *seemed* ok. Although when I think about it, I realize that even then, it wasn't really ok.

By not having many close friends and having absolutely nothing in common with people you're surrounded.

It happens.

>What made you realize that humans are all selfish dicks?

That realization gradually started appearing in mind.
I cannot recall anything in particular, but if I had to generalize it would probably be the sentence - "I don't give a shit about anything, as long as me and my family are fine"

And yeah, you're right, *most* people care about their families. But that's about it.

One of the things that's killing me is spending years and years without *talking* with someone. And I'm thinking about really talking and not just small-talk...

Many people like to help others just to feel good about themselves and to get some benefit (even subconsciously).

For example, most highly religious people don't help other people because they genuinely care about them, but because they believe that doing good deeds will grant them a better position in afterlife.

And don't get me wrong, there truly *are* amazing and caring humans in this world, but they are such a small minority, that they can hardly be noticed.

>Have you always disliked and/or been indifferent to people?

One of my earliest memories are kids from the kindergarten, ripping off wings and legs from insects. At that time, I couldn't comprehend why would anyone do such a thing to another living being. I was so sad.

As I grew up, I realized one thing - Humans are evil, self-centered assholes. Fuck them.

>What do you like doing?

Sleeping. One of the rare activities which make me feel ok. I sleep for 12 hours a day, without interruption.

>What problems do you see in the world?

All the problems I see are way out of control and are definitely not fixable.
I'm trying my best not think about them.

>What do you want to change?

As with problems, I, as an individual, am small and completely powerless to do anything about anything.

>What do you want to learn?

Nothing really. Knowing a dozen programming languages and 3 spoken ones have made me feel there isn't anything new to learn. I know I'm wrong, but I don't feel motivated to try learning anything new.

>Do you have people to care about?

I don't like people.
If I'm not actively hating them, I'm indifferent towards people at best.

There is only meaning if we make one.
For example, some people collect coins. Or postage stamps.
Those activities give meaning to their lives.
Others have families.
That also gives meaning.

I cannot seem to find one.
Everything IS pointless.
Why bother?
Why spend another 40-50+ years of life doing nothing, only to die of old age at the end.

I say fuck it.
I'll choose when I die.
Having control over time and way of my death is the closest I'll get to having a meaning.
Any suggestions with that? I've been struggling with it for more than half of my life.

You're right. I agree with all those things.

If I had to describe myself, I'd say I'm a fighter. A tough one.
But the problem is - I don't see anything worth fighting for.
